question.text: A steel wire of diameter <math><mn>0.5</mn><mi>m</mi><mi>m</mi></math> and Young's modulus <math><mn>2</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mrow><mn>10</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>11</mn></mrow></msup><mi> </mi><mi>N</mi><msup><mrow><mi>m</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math> carries a load of mass M. The length of the wire with the load is 1.0 m. A vernier scale with 10 divisions is attached to the end of this wire. Next to the steel wire is a reference wire to which a main scale, of least count 1.0 mm, is attached. The 10 divisions of the vernier scale correspond to 9 divisions of the main scale. Initially, the zero of vernier scale coincides with the zero of main scale. If the load on the steel wire is increased by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1.2</mn><mo> </mo><mi>k</mi><mi>g</mi></math> , the vernier scale division which coincides with a main scale division is __________. Take <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><mi> </mi><mi>m</mi><msup><mi>s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mi> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">n</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">d</mi><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">π</mi><mo>=</mo><mi> </mi><mn>3.2</mn><mi> </mi><mo>.</mo></math>

solution.text:
d=0.5 mm
Y=2×1011
l=1m
∆l=FlAy=mglπd24y=1.2×10×1π4×5×10-42×2×1011
∆l=1.2×103.24×25×10-8×2×1011
= 121.6×25×103=1240×103=0.03mm
So 3rd division of vernier scale will coincicle with main scale
